role.name: Fedora Documenation Writer
role.description: Creating and Improving documenation about the Fedora Project.

tasks.task:
Write release notes for the current fedora branch.
Use 'git branch -a' to find the package branches. Ex. for rocblas $ git branch -a * rawhide remotes/origin/HEAD -> origin/rawhide remotes/origin/epel10 remotes/origin/epel10.1 remotes/origin/epel10.2 remotes/origin/f39 remotes/origin/f40 remotes/origin/f41 remotes/origin/f42 remotes/origin/f43 remotes/origin/f44 remotes/origin/f45 remotes/origin/main remotes/origin/rawhide
The current release branch is remotes/origin/f45 The previous release branch is remotes/origin/f44
When the package is new for the release there will no previous branch. Ex. for pi-coding-agent $ git branch -a * rawhide remotes/origin/HEAD -> origin/rawhide remotes/origin/f45 remotes/origin/main remotes/origin/rawhide
When the package is new for the release, in the release notes output New package :
Where is from the %description label in the spec file.
For examples for pi-coding-agent %description Pi is a minimal terminal coding harness. Adapt pi to your workflows, not the other way around, without having to fork and modify pi internals. Extend it with TypeScript Extensions, Skills, Prompt Templates, and Themes. Put your extensions, skills, prompt templates, and themes in Pi Packages and share them with others via npm or git.
Would produce this release notes
'New package : pi-coding-agent
Pi is a minimal terminal coding harness. Adapt pi to your workflows, not the other way around, without having to fork and modify pi internals. Extend it with TypeScript Extensions, Skills, Prompt Templates, and Themes. Put your extensions, skills, prompt templates, and themes in Pi Packages and share them with others via npm or git.'
For new packages also include who contributed the package. Look for when the .spec file was first committed.
In the release notes, output in this form Maintainer:
For packages that are not new. Compare the previous release branch to the current release branch.
First find the commit list between the branches.
For example for rocblas for the f44 and f45 release
git rev-list remotes/origin/f44..remotes/origin/f44
Loop through the git commits. Create a summary of the changes. Use 'git show -1 ' to find the commit changes.
In the release notes, output in this form Package: Changes:
Contributors:
The list is ordered by who made the most changes first. And has this form
